questionText: In a 4-bit ripple counter, if the period of the waveform at the last flip-flop is 64 microseconds, then the frequency of the ripple counter in kHz is ________. (Answer in integer)
explanation:
Step 1: Relationship in an $n$-bit Ripple Counter
An $n$-bit ripple counter divides the input clock frequency by $2^n$.
Thus, the output time period ($T_{out}$) at the last flip-flop is related to the input clock period ($T_{in}$) by:
$T_{out} = 2^n \times T_{in}$

Step 2: Calculate the Input Clock Period ($T_{in}$)
For a 4-bit counter ($n = 4$) and $T_{out} = 64\ \mu\text{s}$:
$64\ \mu\text{s} = 2^4 \times T_{in} = 16 \times T_{in}$
$T_{in} = \frac{64}{16} = 4\ \mu\text{s}$

Step 3: Calculate the Input Frequency ($f_{in}$)
The frequency of the input clock to the ripple counter is:
$f_{in} = \frac{1}{T_{in}} = \frac{1}{4\ \mu\text{s}} = 0.25\ \text{MHz} = 250\ \text{kHz}$

Hence, the frequency of the ripple counter is 250 kHz.
